## Choose your execution route

Prerequisites: Original ARENA1.1 module/caching conventions, tensor broadcasting and the scalar recurrence developed here. A fresh CPU learner needs PyTorch and the course dependencies, **no pretrained cache** for the analytic route. Work through dynamics, scans, mixer/model/cache tests and the model-free weight-mapping tests; then run the WRITE/HOLD/READ/ERASE signature and play.

The optional checkpoint route additionally needs the exact `REAL_MAMBA_MODEL_ID` and full `REAL_MAMBA_REVISION` printed in setup cached in advance, plus Transformers' compatible Mamba implementation and sufficient CPU RAM for both130M models. `local_files_only=True` does not acquire missing files. Cache acquisition is a separate deliberate action; no alternate revision is substituted. CUDA release hooks are a third, separately authorized route.

### Practice opens with optional native execution off

The **Practice** workspace defaults `RUN_OPTIONAL_NATIVE=False`. Keep it false for the CPU route. The course reader automatically guards the optional native execution cells in the blank Practice notebook; core function definitions, stubs and all original reference results remain preserved. The Reference notebook retains historical unguarded code and is a reading artifact until its prerequisites are met. In a fresh kernel run Practice setup first, then inspect the flag before continuing. Setting the flag true opts into every guarded native branch in this section; meet all their prerequisites first. No model acquisition occurs with the flag false.

The guard begins at `parity_start`, leaving `hf_to_local_key`, `load_hf_mamba_weights`, `load_pinned_mamba_130m_cpu` and `pinned_mamba_cpu_parity` defined. With the flag false the cached-load tail is skipped, and execution continues at `tests.test_weight_mapping_without_checkpoint` and `tests.test_parity_assembly_without_checkpoint`, then the exact selective-memory signature and WRITE/HOLD/READ/ERASE play. Read saved checkpoint output as historical; your analytic memory result is a separate computation.
